text:
ConocoPhillips jumped 3.55% today to close at $150.80, its highest price in two weeks, as oil prices spiked on escalating Middle East tensions. Brent crude reached $116 a barrel—a six-month high—following Saudi Arabia's interception of Houthi missiles and drones, combined with signals that the U.S. may resume military action against Iran. For an oil major like ConocoPhillips, higher crude prices directly translate to higher profits on the barrels they produce and refine.

The stock's broader two-week gain of 12.45% reflects a sustained rally driven by geopolitical risk premiums pushing global oil prices higher while U.S. natural gas and energy exports benefit from the regional disruption. This trade has been building as Middle East tensions have intensified, rewarding U.S. energy producers with both higher commodity prices and stronger competitive positioning.
